findings.desc: packages/main/src/core/host-run.ts:1056 - FinalAssistantResultScanner.markOversizeCandidate() permanently latches candidateTruncated=true (and increments candidateCount) for any oversize candidate that looks canonical, and no later path ever clears it. Unlike consider(), which resets result/candidateCount/candidateTruncated when ordinary codex prose arrives, the oversize path has no corresponding recovery. Because parseManagedReviewFinalProposal() (managed-host-run.ts:2066) checks finalAssistantResultTruncated FIRST, a provider that emits one oversize canonical chunk and then a perfectly valid bounded proposal is terminated as managed_review_final_result_oversize, discarding valid provider-authored evidence. Verified by direct probe against the built scanner: after an oversize canonical candidate the snapshot is {count:1,truncated:true}; after a subsequent fully valid proposal it becomes {count:2,truncated:true}, so both the truncated and multiple guards reject it. This fails CLOSED (no false pass, no gate bypass) so it is an availability/robustness defect, not an integrity hole - but it silently forces an otherwise-successful managed review round to be re-run.

packages/main/src/core/finding-verify.ts:74-89 - the managed finding signature domain (version 4) covers only desc/severity/timestamp/reviewRound/reviewRunId/managedEvidenceBinding plus read provenance, omitting category, evidenceState, uncertaintyReason and files. The native domain (version 6, lines 56-72) deliberately binds exactly those fields via the nativeFindingSemantics block, so the two authority paths are asymmetric for no stated reason. This is NOT currently exploitable: verifyManagedReviewEvidence().exactEvidenceMatches (managed-review-evidence.ts:255-275) re-digests category/evidenceState/uncertaintyReason/files against the sealed provider proposal, and I confirmed the REVIEW gate always supplies the evidence argument (review-run.ts:1543-1547), so tampering with a managed finding's category is still caught as managed_receipt_invalid. The defect is loss of defense-in-depth: the _hash alone no longer authenticates those provider-authored fields, so any future consumer that validates the signature without also running the receipt-digest check (a new reader, an export path, or a relaxation of the evidence argument to optional) would silently accept mutated finding semantics. Recommend binding the same semantics block in the managed domain for parity.
